correctness.rationale: For arbitrary L² boundary f, choose a simultaneous Lebesgue point of f and |f|². Nontangential convergence makes V_f vanish there. For the disk-algebra normalized perturbation g_r=b_{rζ}+rζ, V_g=1-|b|² and ||g||_G=1. Inverting b shows every fixed-positive superlevel set of V_g approaches ζ uniformly inside a Stolz cone. This forces sup_z min(V_f,V_g)→0, and the centered L² Minkowski inequality gives ||f±g||≤1+sqrt(delta_r)→1. The reverse asymptotic bound comes from the triangle inequality for their sum. All f of norm one and all four spaces are covered; norm<1 points cannot be strongly extreme. No unproved computational step or finite exhaustion is needed.

value.rationale: The recent source explicitly proposes the strong-extremity variant of its Garsia-norm BMO problem. This result gives a complete classification (the empty set) for both BMO and BMOA and simultaneously VMO and VMOA. It separates strong from ordinary extremity maximally: known ordinary extreme behavior of every unit VMO vector coexists with no strongly extreme vectors. The uniform-for-each-f Blaschke localization mechanism is structural and works for unbounded BMO inputs; it is not a routine restatement of any ordinary-extreme theorem.
